ETERNAL
SECURITY
RICK JAMES
I stood there in the bookstore staring, transfixed on the
gold-embossed pentagram on the cover. There it was,
The Satanic Bible—embodiment of evil. Strangely it
was not evil that scared me, but something good, my free
will. I had a terrifying thought “What if I were to recant
my faith and call upon Lucifer.” I had no desire to do that
mind you, I love Christ, but it was the fact that I could,
that it was within my power to throw away heaven, that
was utterly terrifying.
The security and comfort of our salvation is often
short-lived. Mine was anyway. Following on the heels
of my discovery of eternal life came the fear that I
could loose it. In all honesty, I thought more about
that, than I did about my salvation. In point of fact I
became compulsive about it, combing through the
Bible in search of verses to quiet my growing anxiety.
But any verse about salvation, if mentally appendaged
with the clause, “unless I loose it,” not only provides
little comfort, it actually heightens anxiety.
I had salvation, but without security what peace did
that bring me? I was anxious here, now, and felt the
eternal state of my soul was still in jeopardy, for in
theory I had the latent power to relinquish it. I had a
winning lottery ticket—so what—I also had the power
to tear it up.
I grant you that I am a mental basket-case, but
sometimes it takes a basket-case to press a point.
For as the English say, few people ever follow an idea
through to its “ruddy end.” Basket-cases do that.
And that’s where I was, at the ruddy end, which in
walking with God, is never a bad place to be. For
nothing precipitates an intervention from the Lord
like being at the end of ourselves. God starts where we
end.
Well, at this point it would be good to mention that I
no longer struggle with this issue, or the security of
my salvation (I’ve moved on to be compulsive about
other things) and that is due to a few of the following
lessons God taught me in that state of desperation.
A RELATIONSHIP NOT A CONTRACT
Negotiations can be broken off and contracts voided
but relationships are different. In theory, I can tell my
father that I no longer wish to be in his family but in
reality I can never change the fact that I am his son. I
can sever our fellowship but not our relationship.
In John 1:12,13 it says “Yet to all who received him, to
those who believed in his name, he gave the privilege
to become children of God — children born not of
natural descent, nor of human decision or a husband’s
will, but born of God.”
Because I made a decision to place my faith in Christ,
I have been born into the family of God. I cannot
unborn myself, but only use bad grammar to describe
the possibility.
NOT ONE THING
Salvation was a gift. There is not one thing we did to

earn it. Likewise, there is not one thing we can do to
loose it: if there were, our salvation would in some way
be based upon our performance—which it’s not.
GOD WANTS US TO FEEL SECURE
I don’t pretend to think that I am in any way as loving
as God. But, vile creature that I am, I would want my
child (I have several of them) to enjoy the security of
knowing they will always be a part of our family. If I
said to my daughter, “You will always be in the family
provided you don’t (fill in the blank).” Actually let’s
fill in the blank. Let’s say I told her that she would
always be a member of the family as long as she
never touched the Ranch dressing in the refrigerator.
Wouldn’t I have done the exact opposite of giving her
security? In fact all I’ve done is make her terrified of
Ranch dressing.
The world works on the principle, “I will love and
accept you if you do x, y, and z.” A family operates on
the opposite principle: “I love and accept you, now
in gratitude do x, y, and z.” This is grace-motivated
obedience and this is what the gospel is about. For
me, putting the concept of my salvation and security
into the context of my family has helped me to better
understand the security God wants me to have. There
have also been some passages of scripture that God
has used to affirm my security.
THE AUTHORITY OF GOD’S WORD
“And this is the testimony: God has given us eternal life,
and this life is in his Son. He who has the Son has life;
he who does not have the Son of God does not have life. I
write these things to you who believe in the name of the
Son of God so that you may know that you have eternal
life.” (1 John 5:11-13)
It’s important that we take God at his word. In this
passage the apostle John makes it clear that if we have
received Christ, we have eternal life—period. I have
had to stand by faith upon these verses and not allow
anything to pry them away.
SALVATION IS ALSO A PROCESS
“Being confident of this, that he who began a good work
in you will carry it on to completion until the day of
Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 1:6)
“For those God foreknew he also predestined to be
conformed to the likeness of his Son, that he might
be the firstborn among many brothers. And those he
predestined, he also called; those he called, he also
justified; those he justified, he also glorified.”
(Romans 8:29,30)
When you trusted Christ you received eternal life.
But the one-time gift is also a process, as described by
these Bible passages. God has assured us in his word
that the process he began will be completed:
DOES THAT HELP?
“Sort of, but what about…?”
I knew you were going to ask that. What about
passages in the scripture that imply that you need to
persevere in the faith or you may not have eternal life.
Let me give you a strange analogy:
Let’s say I’m a magician. And before your eyes I turn a
dog into a man. Nice trick. You of course are naturally
a little suspicious. Did I really do it? Well, if in fact this
man starts to act like a human than it seems I truly
have acquired quite a neat skill. But, if the man begins
to clean himself, and lap water with his tongue you
would quickly realize it was an illusion. What I had
really done was dress a dog up to look like a man. The
person’s behavior would demonstrate that they were
never actually changed.
A long way to go to make a point—granted—but here
it is. The scriptures are clear that the only way to
know who is changed (born again) is to look to certain
outwards signs of life-change. If these outward signs
are never manifest than you have good reason to
conclude that person is not a possessor of eternal life.
Their actions reveal, not that they lost their salvation,
but that they never possessed it.
One final note to ponder: if you’ve trusted Christ,
the very fact that you are worried about the security
of your salvation is evidence that you have it. A lost
person simply doesn’t care.
Rick James serves as the publisher of CruPress
producing resources for the Campus Ministry
